chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Uthman ibn Isa from Sama'ah ibn Mihran said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who has the fasting of two consecutive months upon him, does he separate the days? He said: 'If he fasts more than a month and connects it, then an event befalls him and he breaks the fast, there is no harm. But if it is less than a month or one month, then he must repeat the fasting.'

key_terms.يُفَرِّقُ بَيْنَ الْأَيَّامِ: to separate the days (break the continuity)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if one breaks the fast of two consecutive months due to an event?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the continuity requirement for expiatory fasting (kaffarat) by distinguishing between partial and substantial completion of the two-month period. The ruling establishes that if the fast is broken after more than a month, the obligation is considered fulfilled despite the interruption, whereas breaking it earlier necessitates a complete restart, reflecting the juristic principle of preserving the integrity of consecutive fasting (muttasil).
